claims.sentence: A scan by GPTZero found 100 fabricated references, most of them to works that do not exist, in 53 papers accepted at NeurIPS 2025 \citep{ansari2026compound}, and a scan of the 2025 papers accepted at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security estimated that 0.38--0.81\% of their references were likely hallucinated \citep{russinovich2026phantom}.
claims.claim: A scan of 2025 accepted papers at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security estimated 0.38-0.81% of references were likely hallucinated.
claims.excerpt:
For the latest complete year, 2025, the all-reference rate is 0.38%
at ICLR, 0.54% at ICML, 0.68% at NeurIPS, and 0.81% at
USENIX Security
claims.note: Supported. Context: rates are over all extracted references (0.31-0.55% over academic-paper-like references); corpus is 'every accepted paper we could retrieve'; 'likely hallucinated' = no matching work found or substantially divergent author list; the authors note false-positive noise dominates at the reference level and call the measured rates an auditable estimate, which 'estimated ... likely' reflects.
